## `ipv64.account`

Your account, its usage and limits, the account log and account links.

### `ipv64.account.me` `GET /me`

```swift
func me() async throws -> Me
```

Shows the plan, usage and limits as well as the credentials used for this request.

### `ipv64.account.logs` `GET /me/logs`

```swift
func logs(limit: Int? = nil, before: Int? = nil, since: Date? = nil) async throws -> IPv64Page<LogEntry, AccountLogMeta>
```

The account log, newest entries first.

### `ipv64.account.links` `GET /me/account-links`

```swift
func links() async throws -> AccountLinks
```

Account links: who may manage your account (`sharedWith`) and which accounts you may manage (`managed`).

## `ipv64.apiKeys`

Manage the API keys of the account.

### `ipv64.apiKeys.list` `GET /api-keys`

```swift
func list() async throws -> [APIKey]
```

Lists all API keys. The keys themselves are never shown again, only their start and end.

### `ipv64.apiKeys.create` `POST /api-keys`

```swift
func create(name: String? = nil, expiresIn: Int? = nil) async throws -> APIKeyCreated
```

Creates an API key. The full key is only contained in this response.

### `ipv64.apiKeys.delete` `DELETE /api-keys/{id}`

```swift
func delete(_ id: Int) async throws
```

Deletes an API key. The key you are currently signed in with cannot delete itself.

## `ipv64.cdn`

CDN: reverse proxy and port mapping for your domains.

### `ipv64.cdn.list` `GET /cdn`

```swift
func list() async throws -> [CDNDomain]
```

Lists all CDN domains.

### `ipv64.cdn.add` `POST /cdn`

```swift
func add(domain: String) async throws -> CDNDomainDetail
```

Adds a domain to the CDN. A CDN server is assigned automatically afterwards.

### `ipv64.cdn.get` `GET /cdn/{token}`

```swift
func get(_ token: String) async throws -> CDNDomainDetail
```

A CDN domain including its port mappings.

### `ipv64.cdn.update` `PATCH /cdn/{token}`

```swift
func update(_ token: String, frontend: CDNFrontend? = nil, backendScheme: CDNBackendScheme? = nil, backendPort: Int? = nil, websocket: Bool? = nil, caching: CDNCachingSettings? = nil, accessList: CDNAccessListSettings? = nil) async throws -> CDNDomainDetail
```

Changes the proxy settings. Only the passed fields are changed. HTTPS in the frontend automatically requests a Let's Encrypt certificate.

### `ipv64.cdn.delete` `DELETE /cdn/{token}`

```swift
func delete(_ token: String) async throws -> CDNDomain
```

Removes a domain from the CDN. Turn the CDN off for all records first.

### `ipv64.cdn.enableProxy` `POST /cdn/{token}/proxy/enable`

```swift
func enableProxy(_ token: String) async throws -> CDNDomain
```

Turns the reverse proxy on. At least one record must run through the CDN.

### `ipv64.cdn.disableProxy` `POST /cdn/{token}/proxy/disable`

```swift
func disableProxy(_ token: String) async throws -> CDNDomain
```

Turns the reverse proxy off.

### `ipv64.cdn.enablePortmapper` `POST /cdn/{token}/portmapper/enable`

```swift
func enablePortmapper(_ token: String) async throws -> CDNDomain
```

Turns the portmapper on. At least one record must run through the CDN.

### `ipv64.cdn.disablePortmapper` `POST /cdn/{token}/portmapper/disable`

```swift
func disablePortmapper(_ token: String) async throws -> CDNDomain
```

Turns the portmapper off.

### `ipv64.cdn.redeploy` `POST /cdn/{token}/redeploy`

```swift
func redeploy(_ token: String) async throws -> CDNDomain
```

Redeploys the configuration.

### `ipv64.cdn.resetTraffic` `POST /cdn/{token}/reset-traffic`

```swift
func resetTraffic(_ token: String) async throws -> CDNDomain
```

Resets the traffic counters of the domain.

### `ipv64.cdn.move` `POST /cdn/{token}/move`

```swift
func move(_ token: String) async throws -> CDNDomain
```

Moves the domain to another CDN server.

### `ipv64.cdn.renewCertificate` `POST /cdn/{token}/renew-certificate`

```swift
func renewCertificate(_ token: String) async throws -> CDNDomain
```

Reissues the certificate. Only with an active proxy and an HTTPS frontend.

## `ipv64.cdn.mappings`

Port mappings of a CDN domain.

### `ipv64.cdn.mappings.list` `GET /cdn/{token}/mappings`

```swift
func list(cdn token: String) async throws -> [CDNMapping]
```

Lists the port mappings.

### `ipv64.cdn.mappings.create` `POST /cdn/{token}/mappings`

```swift
func create(cdn token: String, record: String, targetPort: Int, transport: CDNTransport? = nil, name: String? = nil, listenPort: Int? = nil) async throws -> CDNMapping
```

Creates a port mapping that forwards a public port of the CDN server to a port on your server. Without `listenPort` a free port between 50000 and 62000 is assigned. A and AAAA of the same name with the same target port use the same port.

### `ipv64.cdn.mappings.delete` `DELETE /cdn/{token}/mappings/{mapping}`

```swift
func delete(_ mapping: String, cdn token: String) async throws
```

Deletes a port mapping.

## `ipv64.cloudRouters.publicIPs`

Public IPs of the router.

### `ipv64.cloudRouters.publicIPs.list` `GET /cloud-routers/{token}/public-ips`

```swift
func list(router: String) async throws -> [PublicIP]
```

Lists the public IPs of a router.

### `ipv64.cloudRouters.publicIPs.create` `POST /cloud-routers/{token}/public-ips`

```swift
func create(router: String) async throws -> PublicIP
```

## `ipv64.threat`

Threat intelligence from Honeypot64: IP lookups, statistics, early warning, password check and blocklist feed.

### `ipv64.threat.ip` `GET /threat/ip/{ip}`

```swift
func ip(_ ip: String) async throws -> ThreatIP
```

Why is this IP listed? Returns whether it is listed, its status (including releases), confidence score, lists, kinds, ports (only those reported by at least 2 accounts), first and last sighting, number of reporting accounts, and country/ASN if known. Unlisted IPs have no details.

### `ipv64.threat.stats` `GET /threat/stats`

```swift
func stats() async throws -> ThreatStats
```

Public overview as on the Honeypot64 statistics page: active sensors, attacks in 24 hours, 30-day timeline, top ports and kinds, list sizes, top usernames, passwords, paths, user agents and origin countries. Rankings only contain entries reported by at least `threshold.accounts` accounts. Cached for at most 10 minutes (503 if currently unavailable).

### `ipv64.threat.passwordRange` `GET /threat/passwords/range/{prefix}`

```swift
func passwordRange(prefix: String) async throws -> String
```

Password check with k-anonymity, like the range API of Have I Been Pwned.

### `ipv64.threat.passwordRangeEntries` `GET /threat/passwords/range/{prefix}`

```swift
func passwordRangeEntries(prefix: String) async throws -> [ThreatPasswordRangeEntry]
```

Like `passwordRange(prefix:)`, but parsed into entries. Padding lines (count 0) are included.

### `ipv64.threat.feed` `GET /threat/feed`

```swift
func feed(since: String? = nil) async throws -> ThreatFeed
```

Changes of the v64 Blocklist and its sub-lists since a cursor, oldest first, at most 10 000 per call.

### `ipv64.threat.feed` `GET /threat/feed`

```swift
func feed(since: String?, ifNoneMatch etag: String) async throws -> ThreatFeedResult
```

Conditional variant of `feed(since:)`: sends `If-None-Match` and reports

## `ipv64.threat.watch`

Early warning for your own networks and DynDNS IPs.

### `ipv64.threat.watch.list` `GET /threat/watch`

```swift
func list() async throws -> ThreatWatch
```

Early warning for your networks: limits of your class, registered networks and the automatically watched DynDNS IPs (current public A/AAAA records of your domains).

### `ipv64.threat.watch.add` `POST /threat/watch`

```swift
func add(cidr: String, label: String? = nil) async throws -> ThreatWatchNetwork
```

Registers a public network (CIDR) or a single IP. Host bits are removed (`203.0.113.7/24` becomes `203.0.113.0/24`). Unverified networks (`verified` false) only alert for IPs on the v64 Blocklist.

### `ipv64.threat.watch.delete` `DELETE /threat/watch/{id}`

```swift
func delete(_ id: Int) async throws
```

Removes an own network. Earlier alerts are kept (with their `network_id`).

### `ipv64.threat.watch.alerts` `GET /threat/watch/alerts`

```swift
func alerts(since: String? = nil) async throws -> ThreatWatchAlerts
```

Early-warning alerts: an IP from an own network or a DynDNS IP of the account was flagged as an attacker in the evaluation (every 30 minutes). Oldest first, at most 100 per call. The same IP alerts at most once per 24 hours unless it is newly listed. Alerts are kept for 90 days.
